script: WWII soldiers wore body armor that everyone assumed stopped bullets, and it almost never did. The flak vest was built with steel plates to catch shrapnel from exploding anti-aircraft shells, not gunfire. Against a direct rifle shot, it barely helped at all. Soldiers wore it with total confidence anyway. Real bulletproof vests didn't exist until Kevlar arrived decades later. WWII soldiers wore body armor that couldn't stop the one thing they feared most.
